items.q: How many years is a bachelor's degree in Denmark?
items.a: A university bachelor's degree typically lasts three years, but a professional bachelor's degree can vary between three and four-and-a-half years, depending on the course.

items.q: Can Indian students study a bachelor's degree in Denmark in English?
items.a: Yes, some programmes are taught in English. However, English-taught options vary by subject and institution, so students should check availability for their intended intake. Bachelor in Denmark for Indian students requires checking the language of instruction before choosing a programme.

items.q: What is the tuition fee for a bachelor's degree in Denmark?
items.a: Tuition fees vary depending on the institution and course. For most non-EU/EEA students, a budget of around ₹5 lakh–₹15 lakh or more per year, depending on the programme, should be considered. Always check the current fee on the official university website.

items.q: Is it possible for students to work while studying in Denmark?
items.a: Work rights depend on the student's nationality and residence permit conditions. International students should check the official Danish immigration website for the current rules before taking up employment.

items.q: Can students remain in Denmark after graduation?
items.a: Depending on the qualification, residence permit conditions and immigration rules in force at the time of graduation, post-study options may vary. Students should verify their eligibility requirements with the Danish authorities.
